categories.main_business_segments: Cleanup Corporation's main business segments are the manufacturing and sales of kitchen equipment (system kitchens), bathroom and washstand equipment (system bathrooms and vanities), and related products for residential and commercial facilities. The company also operates logistics, after-sales service, stainless steel processing, IT solutions, and human resource services through its subsidiaries.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company specializes in the design and production of high-quality system kitchens and bathrooms, with a particular focus on stainless steel processing and environmentally conscious materials. Production methods emphasize mass production, VE (Value Engineering) for cost reduction, and the use of recyclable materials. The company also develops proprietary technologies and collaborates with partners for innovative product development.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Cleanup primarily serves residential housing markets, including new home construction and renovation, as well as commercial facilities such as stores and offices. Its key customers are housing developers, construction companies, homebuilders, and end consumers seeking kitchen and bathroom solutions.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company’s operations are predominantly in Japan, which accounts for over 90% of sales and assets. It also has a presence in China through a local subsidiary, but international sales are limited compared to its domestic business.
categories.supply_chain_position: Cleanup operates mainly as a midstream and downstream player in the supply chain, handling the design, manufacturing, and direct sales of finished kitchen and bathroom products. It sources raw materials such as stainless steel from suppliers and delivers finished goods to builders, retailers, and end users.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategically, Cleanup focuses on developing high value-added, differentiated products, strengthening its brand as a specialist manufacturer, and promoting sustainability. R&D priorities include shortening product development cycles, enhancing product functionality and design, and advancing environmental initiatives such as carbon neutrality and recyclable materials. The company is also exploring new lifestyle solutions and disaster-resilient products.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through the sale of manufactured kitchen, bathroom, and washstand products. Additional revenue streams include installation, after-sales services, logistics, and IT solutions provided by group subsidiaries. Revenue is recognized at the point of delivery or completion of installation.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Cleanup is positioned as a leading specialist in the Japanese system kitchen and bathroom market, competing with major domestic manufacturers such as LIXIL, Takara Standard, and Panasonic. The industry is highly competitive, with price competition and rapid product imitation, but Cleanup differentiates itself through quality, innovation, and brand strength.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, Cleanup reported consolidated net sales of approximately 130 billion yen, with operating profit of 2.07 billion yen and net profit attributable to parent company shareholders of 1.72 billion yen. The company has shown modest revenue growth (1.6% year-on-year), improved profitability, and maintains a strong equity ratio above 60%. Employee count is over 3,500 on a consolidated basis.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Cleanup emphasizes high-quality, high-value-added products, particularly in stainless steel system kitchens and bathrooms, offering durability, hygiene, and design appeal. The company’s value proposition includes comprehensive service from product to after-sales support, environmental responsibility, and continuous innovation to meet evolving lifestyle needs.
